title: Field-extension exchange morphism isomorphism
statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension] and let $g:T\to S$ be a quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] morphism of schemes over $K$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. For $W=T,S$ put $W_L=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}L$ and let $r_W:W_L\to W$ be the scalar-extension projection [def-pc-base-change]. Write $g_L:T_L\to S_L$ for the induced base change of $g$, so that the square with sides $g,g_L,r_T,r_S$ is cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].

Let $E\in\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ be a bounded below derived object of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] whose cohomology sheaves have geometric stalks torsion of orders invertible in $K$ [def-kun-torsion-invertible]. Put $E_L=r_T^{-1}E$, using the derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], and use the derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Then the canonical derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] for this cartesian field-extension square,
$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{g,L,E}:r_S^{-1}Rg_*E\longrightarrow Rg_{L,*}E_L,
$$
is an isomorphism in $\Dplus((S_L)_{\Et})$.

source.place: Lemma 0F1C (lemma-base-change-field-extension), statement and proof: the smooth-base-change comparison map for the field-extension square

proof.text:
First record the coefficient condition under scalar extension. For a field extension $M/K$ and a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T_M$, [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition], and [lem-kun-stalks-of-cohomology] give
$$\mathcal H^q(r_T^{-1}E)_{\bar t}\cong\mathcal H^q(E)_{r_T\bar t}.$$
Indeed the derived stalk is inverse image by $\bar t$, its composite with $r_T^{-1}$ is inverse image by $r_T\bar t$, and taking degree $q$ gives the formula. Thus the same positive integers annihilate the corresponding stalk elements. An integer invertible in $K$ stays invertible in $M$, and its constant image is invertible in $\Gamma(S_M,\mathcal O_{S_M})$ by applying the structural ring map to its inverse in $M$. The inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] preserves bounded below objects. No uniform annihilator, finite coefficient ring, or constructibility is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F1C, lemma-base-change-field-extension, coefficient condition; inverse-image composition and geometric stalk calculation

proof.text: Suppose first that $L/K$ is separable. By [lem-kun-separable-smooth-colimit] write $L=\varinjlim_{i\in I}A_i$ over the set of smooth finitely generated $K$-subalgebras of $L$, ordered by inclusion. This is a nonempty directed set and $\operatorname{Spec}L=\varprojlim_i\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with affine transitions. Put $S_i=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. The structure morphisms $S_i\to S$ are smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The only opens of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ are the empty open and the whole scheme, whose inverse images are the empty affine scheme and $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is affine directly by the definition, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], clauses (1) and (3), makes $S_i\to S$ affine, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $i\le j$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}A_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is an affine transition supplied by [lem-kun-separable-smooth-colimit]; $S_j\to S_i$ is its base change along $S_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, so clause (1) of the affine-permanence node makes it affine. These statements do not require $S$ or $T$ themselves to be quasi-compact.

proof.text: The inverse limit of the $S_i$ is $S_L$. To check this without a quasi-compactness hypothesis on $S$, a compatible cone $Z\to S_i$ gives one map $Z\to S$ (all these components agree by directedness) and a compatible cone $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, hence one map $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. Their composites to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ agree, so the fibre-product universal property gives a unique $Z\to S_L$, and conversely such a map gives the cone. Apply [lem-kun-0f09] with its base scheme equal to the given $S$, its direct-image leg $f$ equal to $g:T\to S$, and its smooth inverse system equal to $(S_i\to S)$. Its limit square is exactly the square of the statement: $T\times_S S_L=T_L$. The leg $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by assumption; for every stalk element the annihilating integer is a unit on $S$ because it is a unit in $K$. All the hypotheses of that node hold, so its conclusion is precisely that the canonical map $\operatorname{Ex}_{g,L,E}$ is invertible when $L/K$ is separable. In particular the direct-image leg here is not the structural morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$.

proof.text:
Now construct compatible perfect closures. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-purely-inseparable-overfield] to $L$ to choose a perfect purely inseparable extension $L'/L$. In characteristic zero take $K'=K$ and $L'=L$. In characteristic $p>0$, regard $K\subseteq L\subseteq L'$ and set
$$K'=\{x\in L':x^{p^n}\in K\text{ for some }n\ge0\}.$$
This is a subfield: for two elements choose one exponent at least as large as both exponents, and use $(x+y)^{p^N}=x^{p^N}+y^{p^N}$, $(xy)^{p^N}=x^{p^N}y^{p^N}$, and $(x^{-1})^{p^N}=(x^{p^N})^{-1}$ for $x\ne0$. The extension $K'/K$ is purely inseparable by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Every $x\in K'$ has a $p$th root $y\in L'$ by perfection of $L'$; if $x^{p^n}\in K$, then $y^{p^{n+1}}\in K$, so $y\in K'$. Thus $K'$ is perfect as well. We have a commutative square of inclusions $K\subseteq K'\subseteq L'$ and $K\subseteq L\subseteq L'$ with both $K'/K$ and $L'/L$ purely inseparable.

source.place: Tags 046W and 046X, lemma-perfection and definition-perfection; compatible realization inside the chosen perfect closure, expanding the choice in Tag 0F1C

proof.text: The extension $L'/K'$ is separable in the possibly transcendental sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. In fact take any intermediate field $K'\subseteq F\subseteq L'$ finitely generated over $K'$. Since $K'$ has characteristic zero or surjective Frobenius, [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis] applied to $F/K'$ gives a finite transcendence basis over which $F$ is separable algebraic. This says that $F/K'$ is separably generated. Applying the definition to every such $F$ proves the assertion. This does not claim that $L'/K'$ is algebraic or finitely generated.

proof.text: For $W=T,S$ write $a_W:W_{K'}\to W$ and $c_W:W_{L'}\to W_L$ for the projections induced by $K'/K$ and $L'/L$. These four maps are universal homeomorphisms, not merely homeomorphisms. Indeed, for any $K$-scheme $Z\to W$, the base change of $a_W$ is $Z_{K'}\to Z$, a homeomorphism by [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep]; the fibre-product identification follows directly from its universal property. For any morphism $Z\to W_L$, regard $Z$ as an $L$-scheme. The base change of $c_W$ along this morphism is $Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}L}\operatorname{Spec}L'\to Z$ by the fibre-product universal property. Since $L'/L$ is purely inseparable, [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] says that this projection is a homeomorphism. Since this works for every base change, it is exactly [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism].

proof.text: By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] the inverse images along $a_T,a_S,c_T,c_S$ are equivalences on etale sheaves, compatible with the indicated functors. They also give equivalences on abelian sheaves: the inverse functors transport the zero object, finite products, and the abelian-group operations, and inverse images transport these operations back. On abelian categories these equivalences and their quasi-inverses are exact, since a categorical equivalence transports the universal properties of kernels and cokernels. Apply them termwise to complexes. They preserve cohomology and hence quasi-isomorphisms and bounded below cohomology, and their termwise units and counits remain inverse natural isomorphisms after localization. This explicitly gives mutually inverse functors on the bounded below derived categories defined in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The forward functors are the derived inverse images of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], whose definition is exactly termwise inverse image followed by localization.

proof.text: Let $b_W:W_{L'}\to W_{K'}$ be the projections for $L'/K'$, and put $E_{K'}=a_T^{-1}E$. Both $g_{K'}$ and $g_L$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. By Step 1, $E_{K'}$ satisfies the required boundedness and torsion condition over $K'$. Steps 2--3 applied to the separable extension $L'/K'$ therefore prove that $\operatorname{Ex}_{b,E_{K'}}:b_S^{-1}Rg_{K',*}E_{K'}\to Rg_{L',*}b_T^{-1}E_{K'}$ is an isomorphism. Moreover the canonical exchanges $\operatorname{Ex}_{a}$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_{c}$ are natural isomorphisms for all bounded below objects, independently of torsion. To verify the latter assertion for $a$, apply [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] with $L=g^{-1}$, $R=Rg_*$, $L'=g_{K'}^{-1}$, $R'=Rg_{K',*}$, $G=a_S^{-1}$ and $G'=a_T^{-1}$. The two adjunctions are those of [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction]; both horizontal inverse images are equivalences by Step 7, so $G$ is an equivalence and $G'$ is fully faithful as required. The isomorphism $\theta:L'G\cong G'L$ is the inverse-image square isomorphism. By [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] its mate is exactly $\operatorname{Ex}_a$, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of its source and target. For $c$, instantiate that mate lemma with $L=g_L^{-1}$, $R=Rg_{L,*}$, $L'=g_{L'}^{-1}$, $R'=Rg_{L',*}$, $G=c_S^{-1}$ and $G'=c_T^{-1}$. The derived-adjunction node supplies these two adjunctions. Step 7 makes $c_S^{-1}$ an equivalence and $c_T^{-1}$ fully faithful. The inverse-image square isomorphism is $g_{L'}^{-1}c_S^{-1}\cong c_T^{-1}g_L^{-1}$, and its mate is $\operatorname{Ex}_c$ by the exchange definition. The lemma therefore makes $\operatorname{Ex}_c$ a natural isomorphism on all bounded below objects.
